item.text: {"search_note":"I found no direct 2024 evidence that Kishida had to resist nuclear proliferation pressure from a domestic faction, proxy, or ally in the narrow political-interest sense. The best-fitting evidence is about North Korea nonproliferation, NPT/FMCT diplomacy, and containment through alliance coordination. So the strongest defensible reading is: yes, Kishida resisted proliferation in the regional/international nonproliferation sense; evidence is sparse for the more specific ally/faction-pressure formulation.","evidence":[{"title":"Address by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Ceremony","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"August 6, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/06hiroshima.html","summary":"Kishida said Japan should uphold the Three Non-Nuclear Principles, maintain and strengthen the NPT regime, and push practical measures to stop any reversal in the downward trend in nuclear weapons. He also launched the FMCT “Friends” framework as part of that effort.","question_ids":["1B.6","1B.4","1B.1"]},{"title":"Press Conference by the Prime Minister regarding His Attendance at the 2024 Peace Memorial Ceremony in Hiroshima and Other Matters","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"August 6, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/06kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida said the NPT is the place for nuclear and non-nuclear states to sit at the same table and that Japan must involve nuclear-weapon states in concrete activities to change reality. That is direct evidence of resisting proliferation through multilateral diplomacy rather than tolerating it for convenience.","question_ids":["1B.6","1B.4","1B.1","1B.2"]},{"title":"Address by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio at the Nagasaki Peace Memorial Ceremony","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"August 9, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/09nagasaki.html","summary":"Kishida again called the NPT the cornerstone of nonproliferation and said Japan would continue to seek concrete measures that nuclear-weapon states and non-nuclear-weapon states can take together. This shows sustained, not episodic, resistance to proliferation.","question_ids":["1B.6","1B.4"]},{"title":"The Ninth Japan-China-ROK Trilateral Summit (Summary)","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"May 27, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202405/27chnrok.html","summary":"Kishida expressed serious concern over North Korea’s nuclear and missile activities, the Russia-North Korea relationship, and urged North Korea to completely abandon its nuclear and ballistic missile programs in line with UN Security Council resolutions. This is the clearest 2024 evidence that he resisted regional proliferation.","question_ids":["1B.6","1B.4","1B.5"]},{"title":"Japan-U.S. Summit Meeting (Summary)","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"April 10, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202404/10usa.html","summary":"Kishida and President Biden discussed North Korea’s nuclear and missile development and Russia-North Korea relations, and Kishida sought continued U.S. support on the abductions issue. While not a direct anti-proliferation pledge, it shows Kishida using alliance diplomacy to contain North Korean proliferation rather than accommodate it.","question_ids":["1B.6","1B.4"]},{"title":"Address by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio at a Joint Meeting of the United States Congress","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"April 11, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202404/11speech.html","summary":"Kishida emphasized Japan’s counterstrike capability, defense buildup, and stronger U.S. extended deterrence. That is indirect negative evidence: he did not break with allied deterrence arrangements even while promoting disarmament language.","question_ids":["1B.6","1B.4","1B.1"]}]}
